title: Opening a second unit steals the first unit's phase node, emptying its run DAG and its exported canvas
command:
export BATTEN_DB=.../run-ws/state.db
batten phase US-012 build
batten hook SubagentStart <<< '{"session_id":"s3","cwd":"<repo>","agent_id":"C1","agent_type":"backend"}'
batten show US-012 ; batten canvas US-012 --out us012-before.canvas
batten phase US-013 build          # a second session opens another unit
batten show US-012 ; batten canvas US-012 --out us012-after.canvas
observed:
=== BEFORE — US-012's DAG:
US-012  run=US-012-1785220349240324700-346df4be  status=running  phase=build  base=44630cd
  [phase] build                    running 
  [subagent] backend                  running 
wrote .../us012-before.canvas (4 nodes, 1 edges)

=== a second session opens ANOTHER unit: batten phase US-013 build

=== AFTER — US-012's DAG:
US-012  run=US-012-1785220349240324700-346df4be  status=running  phase=build  base=44630cd
  [subagent] backend                  running 
wrote .../us012-after.canvas (1 nodes, 0 edges)
expected: US-012's DAG should be unaffected by anything US-013 does. Node ids must be namespaced per run. `AddNode` does `INSERT OR REPLACE` on a globally-unique `node_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY`, and `cmdPhase` builds that id as `"p-" + phaseID` with no run in it — so every `batten phase <any-unit> build` in a shared DB moves the single row `p-build` to the newest run. The effect ping-pongs: re-running `batten phase US-002 build` moved the node back to US-002 (canvas 1→4 nodes) and simultaneously emptied US-003 (4→1). It also survived a run being closed: US-001, closed and rolled_back, still exported an empty canvas.
file_hint: cmd/batten/main.go (cmdPhase, `NodeID: "p-" + phaseID` ~line 368) and internal/store/store.go (AddNode INSERT OR REPLACE ~line 404)
